original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Accelerate the exact sparse integer-dyadic row kernels in incorporated PR917's four complete CK scalar streams, preserving the entire historical verifier through an opt-in adapter.
scope_change_reason: Seed 89 selects verification engineering. Three candidate objects were screened; 89 mod 3 selects the measured CK sparse-row bottleneck. This is verification throughput for a historical circuit, not a proposed multiplication mechanism.
bottleneck_link: Exact replay is reused when reviewing finite circuit candidates. The measured row kernels consume about half the integer-replay time; faster complete checks increase that stage's throughput with identical coverage.
stop_rule: One kernel implementation; abandon if any exact comparison or retained fault control fails, or five alternating same-input benchmark pairs show no useful stage acceleration. At most 20 percent orientation; reserve final 25 percent for verification and handoff.
evidence: RESULT.json records every-kernel/full-stream comparisons, arithmetic and drift controls and the unchanged complete PR917 receipt. BENCHMARK.json and BENCHMARK-PY312.json separately record five paired timings per interpreter and identical input/result hashes. Python 3.12 registered replay and Python 3.14 optimized full verification pass. VERIFY.json registers the complete bounded replay.
author: Sricharan Vagvala (@theon199)
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance for selection, implementation, arithmetic analysis, testing, verification and writing. Parent-only execution; no independent human review.

open_questions.question: Does the same kernel adapter improve another source-bound dyadic scalar replay with a larger arithmetic share?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The measured 1.50x improvement applies only to PR917's integer stage; most complete-replay time is outside that stage.
open_questions.first_step: Profile one other dyadic replay, prove its zero-free immutable-row invariant, then compare its complete primitive streams and controls before applying these kernels.
open_questions.blocked_by: A separately pinned target and complete coverage review; this package does not automatically replace any compiler or verifier.
